note: Technical validation only; no human approval or original-protocol reproduction.

cases.reason: External unbounded input reaches narrowing without a guard; an input of 2^128 succeeds but is stored as zero.
cases.requirement: A successful record(amount) must store the complete amount.

cases.reason: The only path checks the original amount before casting. Accepted values are in range; rejected transactions leave reserve unchanged.
cases.requirement: Store the complete accepted amount; revert for amounts outside uint128.

cases.reason: Both guarded and unguarded full programs are compatible with this exact fragment; do not assign a positive or negative verdict from syntax alone.
cases.requirement: Cannot determine reachability or exact-value requirements from the fragment alone.

historical_knowledge.scope: Historical report motivating this pattern; synthetic cases do not reproduce the original protocol.

detection_signals.text: A uint128(...) cast into accounting state is a candidate signal. Confirm it only after tracing the cast expression, incoming paths, range restrictions and downstream exactness requirement.

exploit_conditions.text: In the unsafe synthetic case, anyone can call record(2^128); the transaction succeeds and stores zero, violating the exact-recording requirement. No financial exploit is claimed by this fixture.

impact.text: The fixture demonstrates corrupted accounting values. The historical Caviar finding describes possible reserve/pricing invariant disruption; economic loss and severity require analysis of the target protocol's downstream use and reachable state.

limitations.text: A dominating bound or a proven caller/type invariant can make the cast safe for this pattern. The supplied guarded contract has one entry path and checks the same unchanged amount immediately before conversion.
An internal fragment without its callers and state declaration is insufficient for either confirmation or rejection: the same fragment behaves differently with guarded and unguarded callers.

Intentional modulo behavior is outside this pattern's exact-value requirement. Intent must be supported by design and downstream invariants, not inferred from an unchecked block or a code comment alone.

This card covers unsigned uint256-to-uint128 conversion only. The tests do not establish whole-contract security, financial severity, or the original Caviar PoC. Finite tests are supplemented by the guard's local range argument.

observed_behavior.text: For the tested unsafe contracts, the stored result is amount modulo 2^128. Boundary 2^128-1 is preserved; 2^128 becomes zero and 2^128+1 becomes one.

preconditions.text: The conversion target is uint128, the original value is uint256, and the affected operation requires exact value preservation rather than intentional modulo arithmetic.
There is a reachable path on which the actual expression being cast can exceed 2^128-1. A large declared input type alone does not prove this path exists.

remediation.text: Check the original wide expression against type(uint128).max before narrowing on every reachable path, then reject out-of-range inputs or use a reviewed checked conversion. A check applied to an already truncated value is insufficient.

root_cause.text: Explicit narrowing discards bits above bit 127. A successful cast therefore need not preserve its uint256 input; ordinary checked arithmetic does not supply a range check for this conversion.

pattern.scope: Unsigned uint256 converted to uint128 where successful processing must preserve the complete input value. Not all narrowing casts are vulnerabilities.
pattern.title: Unchecked uint256 to uint128 narrowing in exact-value accounting
